rationale:
Split. The supplied proof (steps 0–7) bundles six separable obligations. Each is a reusable lemma about linear maps, measures, charts or rectifiable triples, and none restates the selected theorem.
- gram_det_lower_bound (new): c^k ≤ √det(⟨Te_i, Te_j⟩) whenever |Ts| ≥ c|s|. This is the Jacobian bound of (6a).
- signed_change_of_variables (new): the signed area formula of (6b)(β), for an integrable real h through an injective Lipschitz–antilipschitz chart.
- chart_orientation (new): a measurable σ = ±1 with JΦ·ξ(Φ) = σ·simpleNVector(∂Φ) a.e. on Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M). This is the pointwise formula of (6c) plus the measurability needed in (6d).
- chart_representation (new): steps (6a)–(6d). For a null-measurable G ⊆ M ∩ Φ(Ω) with θ integrable on G, one ψ ∈ L¹(Ω) gives ∫_G θ(A_#ξ)(α∘f) dH^k = ∫_Ω ψ·α(f∘Φ)(∂(f∘Φ)) for every admissible (f, A, α). The same ψ serves the C¹ integrands (f = g_j, A = Dg_j) and the limit integrand (f = g, A = L).
- integrand_bound (new): steps 2–3. θ·(A_#ξ)(β) is a.e.-strongly measurable and bounded by Λ^k‖β‖θ whenever A is Λ-bounded on weighted tangent spaces.
- partition_tannery (new): steps 5 and 7. Dominated convergence of set integrals along a countable a.e.-partition (countable additivity plus Tannery).

Six comparator-accepted declarations are reused by name. Their titles, statements and Lean types are byte-identical to dag.json:

- chart_change_of_variables, used by signed_change_of_variables and chart_representation;

PARENT ASSEMBLY. This is what deformation_ipl_chart_convergence proves after its children. It uses the node's existing dependencies c1_cover, chart_chain_rule, minor_weak_continuity and pushforward_measurable, which stay outside this split; they are unchanged and only appear in the assembly.
(1) Step 1. Take K := closed 1-neighbourhood of tsupport ω (IsCompact.cthickening) and j₀ with dist(g, g_j) < 1 (Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff). Both integrands vanish off g⁻¹(K) for j ≥ j₀.
(2) Steps 2–3. Apply integrand_bound twice.
 - With A = Dg_j and β = ω∘g_j: bound Λ′ from norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; measurability from pushforward_measurable with f = g_j, L = Dg_j.
 - With A = L and β = ω∘g: bound Λ from HasDerivAt.le_of_lipschitz on t ↦ g(x + tv); measurability from pushforward_measurable.
 The dominator max(Λ, Λ′)^k·sup‖ω‖·1_{g⁻¹(K)}·θ is integrable on M by hypothesis.
(3) Step 4. c1_cover and chart_image_measurable give the pieces E_i := disjointed(M ∩ Φ_i(Ω_i)). They are null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.disjointed), pairwise disjoint, and M = ⋃_i E_i a.e.
(4) Step 6. For each i, chart_representation with G := E_i ∩ g⁻¹(K) gives ψ_i. Its derivative hypothesis comes from the C¹ chain rule for g_j and from chart_chain_rule for (g, L). For j ≥ j₀ both piece integrals equal ∫_{Ω_i} ψ_i·ω(u)(∂u), with u = g_j∘Φ_i resp. u = g∘Φ_i. Then minor_weak_continuity with C := max(Λ, Λ′)·K_i gives convergence on each piece.
(5) Step 7. partition_tannery concludes.

--- Verbatim accepted proof ---

Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

Throughout, G(v) := (⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is the Gram matrix of v = (v₁,…,v_n) and, for a real n×n matrix B and τ = (τ₁,…,τ_n), (Bτ)_i := Σ_j B_ij τ_j. This is item (P1) of the parent proof.

1. (Second identity: change of frame.) Let α be any n-covector. By multilinearity,
 α(Bτ) = Σ_{g : Fin n → Fin n} (Π_i B_{i g(i)}) · α(τ_{g(1)}, …, τ_{g(n)}).
 If g is not injective two arguments coincide and the term vanishes because α is alternating. If g = σ is a permutation, α(τ∘σ) = sign(σ) α(τ). Hence α(Bτ) = (Σ_σ sign(σ) Π_i B_{iσ(i)}) α(τ) = det(B) α(τ) by the Leibniz formula (det B = det Bᵀ, so the row/column convention is immaterial). As this holds for every α, simpleNVector(Bτ) = det(B) • simpleNVector τ. For n = 0 both sides are the functional α ↦ α(∅) and the determinant of the empty matrix is 1.

2. (Gram matrices transform by congruence.) G(Bτ)_{ik} = ⟨Σ_j B_ij τ_j, Σ_l B_kl τ_l⟩ = (B G(τ) Bᵀ)_{ik}; hence det G(Bτ) = det(B)² det G(τ).

3. (Upper bound for orthonormal families.) If τ is orthonormal then |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|τ_i| = ‖α‖ for every α, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≤ 1.

4. (Lower bound for orthonormal families.) Let τ be orthonormal (n ≥ 1), W := span τ and π_W the orthogonal projection onto W. Define α₀(u₁,…,u_n) := det(⟨u_i, τ_j⟩)_{i,j}. It is n-linear and alternating (a determinant whose i-th row depends linearly on u_i, and two equal u's give two equal rows) and continuous (finite dimension). The i-th row (⟨u_i,τ_j⟩)_j is the coordinate vector of π_W u_i in the orthonormal basis τ, of Euclidean length |π_W u_i| ≤ |u_i|. By Hadamard's inequality |det A| ≤ Π_i |row_i(A)| (proof: if the rows are dependent det A = 0; otherwise Gram–Schmidt on the rows gives A = R O with O orthogonal and R lower triangular with diagonal entries |a_i^⊥| ≤ |a_i|, a_i^⊥ the component of the i-th row orthogonal to the previous rows, so |det A| = Π|a_i^⊥| ≤ Π|a_i|; in Lean this is `Orientation.abs_volumeForm_apply_le` for the volume form of W composed with π_W) we get |α₀(u)| ≤ Π|u_i|, i.e. ‖α₀‖ ≤ 1. Since α₀(τ) = det(⟨τ_i,τ_j⟩) = det I = 1, ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≥ |simpleNVector τ (α₀)| / ‖α₀‖ ≥ 1. Together with step 3: ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1 = det G(τ). For n = 0, 0-covectors are the constants c = α(∅) with ‖α‖ = |c|, so ‖simpleNVector ∅‖ = 1 = det of the empty matrix.

5. (Dependent families.) If v₁,…,v_n are linearly dependent then α(v) = 0 for every alternating α (`AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent`), so simpleNVector v = 0 and ‖simpleNVector v‖² = 0. Also G(v) is singular: for a nontrivial c with Σ_j c_j v_j = 0 we get G(v)c = (⟨v_i, Σ_j c_j v_j⟩)_i = 0, so det G(v) = 0. The first identity holds. (This covers in particular n > P.)

6. (Independent families.) If v is linearly independent, Gram–Schmidt produces an orthonormal τ with span τ = span v and v = Bτ, B_ij = ⟨v_i, τ_j⟩, B invertible. By step 1, simpleNVector v = det(B) • simpleNVector τ, so by step 4, ‖simpleNVector v‖ = |det B|. By step 2 and G(τ) = I, det G(v) = det(B)². Hence ‖simpleNVector v‖² = det G(v) = det (Matrix.of fun i j => ⟨v_i, v_j⟩).

Steps 5–6 give the first conjunct for every v; step 1 gives the second conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: Leibniz expansion and the alternating property give α(Bτ) = det(B)·α(τ) for every n-covector α, hence simpleNVector(Bτ) = det(B)•simpleNVector τ.
Gram matrices transform by congruence: det G(Bτ) = det(B)²·det G(τ).
For orthonormal τ: ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≤ Π|τ_i| = 1, and the covector det(⟨u_i,τ_j⟩) has norm ≤ 1 by Hadamard and value 1 at τ, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1.
Dependent families: simpleNVector v = 0 and det G(v) = 0.
Independent families: Gram–Schmidt v = Bτ gives ‖simpleNVector v‖ = |det B| and det G(v) = det(B)².

This lemma combines item (P4)(a),(b) of the parent proof with Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4/1.7, the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” and Remark 1.8(1) (printed arguments, specialized to one C¹ chart), as used in Steps 1, 5.3 and 7 of the parent proof. Setting: V ⊆ ℝ^Q open, M ⊆ V Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, θ Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ V; Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q of class C¹, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Φ c-antilipschitz on Ω (c > 0). Put N := Φ(Ω). Recall η_{y,λ}(z) := λ⁻¹(z − y) (`blowUpMap y λ`) and that HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y P means: dim P = n and for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q), ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_P φ dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0. If n > Q then Hⁿ ≡ 0 on ℝ^Q (Hausdorff dimension of ℝ^Q is Q; `hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt`) and there is nothing to prove; assume n ≤ Q.

0. (Preliminaries on the chart.)
 (a) For w ∈ Ω and s ∈ ℝⁿ: w + ts ∈ Ω for small t, and |Φ(w+ts) − Φ(w)| ≥ c|t||s|; dividing by |t| and letting t → 0 gives |DΦ(w)s| ≥ c|s|. So DΦ(w) is injective and T_w := DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w) has dimension n. Φ is injective on Ω; for y ∈ N let w_y ∈ Ω be the unique point with Φ(w_y) = y, and T_y := T_{w_y}. (The Lean conclusion “∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = y → …” concerns exactly w = w_y.)
 (b) Ψ := (Φ|Ω)⁻¹ : N → Ω is (1/c)-Lipschitz. N is σ-compact (Ω is a countable union of compact sets and Φ is continuous), hence Borel; M ∩ N is Hⁿ-null-measurable.
 (c) N is locally Hⁿ-finite: if K ⊆ ℝ^Q is compact, Ψ(N ∩ K) has diameter ≤ diam(K)/c, so lies in a closed ball B̄ ⊆ ℝⁿ; Φ is Lipschitz on B̄ (C¹ on a compact convex set), say with constant Λ, and Hⁿ(N ∩ K) ≤ Λⁿ Lⁿ(B̄) < ∞.
 (d) (Change of variables under blow-ups.) η_{y,λ} is a similarity of ratio λ⁻¹, so for every set S and every g ≥ 0 or Hⁿ⌞S-integrable g: ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} g dHⁿ = λ^{−n} ∫_S g∘η_{y,λ} dHⁿ (translation invariance and μHE[n](λS) = λⁿ μHE[n](S), Mathlib `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀`).
 (e) (C¹ blow-up of N; Simon: “since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim ∫_{η(N_j)} f = ∫_{T N_j} f”.) For every y ∈ N and φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q): lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ. Proof: let spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), w := w_y. By (d) and the injective area formula for Φ on Ω (Φ injective, Lipschitz on bounded subsets of Ω; Simon Ch. 2 (3.2)/(3.5), SimonGMT `injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn` and its weighted fibre-sum form) the integral equals λ^{−n} ∫_Ω φ((Φ(v) − y)/λ) JΦ(v) dv, JΦ(v) := √det(DΦ(v)*DΦ(v)), and the substitution v = w + λs turns it into I_λ := ∫ 1_{(Ω−w)/λ}(s) φ((Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w))/λ) JΦ(w+λs) ds. If the integrand is nonzero then w, w + λs ∈ Ω and |Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w)| < λR, so c|λs| < λR, i.e. |s| < R/c. For λ ≤ 1 the integrand is bounded by sup|φ| · max_{|z−w| ≤ R/c} JΦ(z) and vanishes for |s| ≥ R/c; for fixed s, as λ ↓ 0: w + λs ∈ Ω eventually (Ω open), (Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w))/λ → DΦ(w)s and JΦ(w+λs) → JΦ(w). By dominated convergence I_λ → ∫_{ℝⁿ} φ(DΦ(w)s) JΦ(w) ds = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ, the last equality being the linear area formula for the injective linear map DΦ(w) (Simon Ch. 2 (3.1); Mathlib `LinearMap.hausdorffMeasure_image`/normDet). Note that for nonnegative φ ≥ 1_{B_R(0)} this also shows sup_{0<λ≤1} λ^{−n} Hⁿ(N ∩ B_{λR}(y)) < ∞.
 (f) (Upper Density Theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT `Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6`.) If μ is a Borel regular measure on ℝ^Q and A is μ-measurable with μ(A) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ ℝ^Q ∖ A, lim_{ρ↓0} ρ^{−n} μ(A ∩ B_ρ(y)) = 0. (Finite Borel measures on ℝ^Q, and Hⁿ restricted to sets of finite measure, are Borel regular.)

1. (Compact pieces with continuous weight — Remark 1.8(1).) Let V_1 ⊆ V_2 ⊆ ⋯ be open sets with compact closures closure V_i ⊆ V_{i+1} ⊆ V and ⋃_i V_i = V. Fix i. ν_i(B) := ∫_{B ∩ M ∩ V_i} θ dHⁿ defines a finite Borel measure (∫_{M ∩ closure V_i} θ < ∞), and θ is ν_i-measurable (θ is a.e. strongly measurable on M ∩ closure V_i by `IntegrableOn`). Choose a Borel M_i′ ⊆ M ∩ V_i with Hⁿ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ M_i′) = 0. For each j ≥ 1, Lusin's theorem for the finite Borel measure ν_i (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT `Chapter01.Lusin`) gives a closed F with ν_i(ℝ^Q ∖ F) < 1/(2j) and θ|F continuous, and inner regularity gives a compact C_{i,j} ⊆ M_i′ ∩ F with ν_i((M_i′ ∩ F) ∖ C_{i,j}) < 1/(2j). As M = ⋃_i (M ∩ V_i), it suffices to prove: for each fixed C := C_{i,j}, the conclusion holds at Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N. Note that θ ≥ m_C := min_C θ > 0 on C (continuous positive function on a compact set), so Hⁿ(C) ≤ m_C^{−1} ∫_C θ dHⁿ < ∞.

 ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ = ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N)} φ − ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N ∖ C)} φ + ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C ∖ N)} φ,
 and |∫_{η_{y,λ}(N∖C)} φ| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0, |∫_{η_{y,λ}(C∖N)} φ| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0, while the first term tends to ∫_{T_y} φ by (e). Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Eucl P with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, = μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)); on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`). B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ. η_{y,λ}(x) = λ⁻¹(x − y) is `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y λ`. ∫_A f dHⁿ is the Bochner set integral (0 when f is not integrable on A); ∫⁻ is the [0,∞]-valued lintegral. 'T is the approximate tangent space of S at y' means `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T` (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T` (Def. 1.7) means finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ).

This is items 0(b) (measurability) and 0(c) (local finiteness) of the parent proof.

1. (Injectivity.) If w, w′ ∈ Ω and Φ(w) = Φ(w′), then c|w − w′| ≤ 0, so w = w′. Thus Φ is injective on Ω.

2. (Borel image.) Ω is open, hence Borel, in the Polish space ℝⁿ, and Φ is continuous (C¹) and injective on Ω. By the Lusin–Souslin theorem, the image of a Borel set under a map that is continuous and injective on it is Borel (Mathlib `MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn`). Hence Φ(Ω) is Borel. (Alternatively, avoiding Lusin–Souslin: Ω is the countable union of the compact closed balls with rational centres and radii contained in Ω, so Φ(Ω) is a countable union of compact, hence closed, sets. `MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn` lives in Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.Polish.Basic, which may need to be imported.)

3. (Localization.) Let K ⊆ ℝ^Q be compact. If Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = ∅ then Φ(Ω) ∩ K = ∅ and Hⁿ(∅) = 0. Otherwise fix w₀ ∈ Ω with Φ(w₀) ∈ K and put D := diam K < ∞. For every v ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K), c|v − w₀| ≤ |Φ(v) − Φ(w₀)| ≤ D, so v ∈ B̄ := B̄_{D/c}(w₀) ⊆ ℝⁿ. Every point of Φ(Ω) ∩ K is Φ(v) for such a v, so Φ(Ω) ∩ K ⊆ Φ(B̄).

4. (Lipschitz bound on B̄.) Φ is C¹, so v ↦ DΦ(v) is continuous and therefore bounded on the compact set B̄: there is Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 with ‖DΦ(v)‖ ≤ Λ for all v ∈ B̄. B̄ is convex, so by the mean value inequality Φ is Λ-Lipschitz on B̄ (Mathlib `Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le`, using differentiability of Φ at every point).

5. (Hausdorff measure of the image.) For a map that is Λ-Lipschitz on B̄, μH[n](Φ(B̄)) ≤ Λⁿ · μH[n](B̄) (`LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le` with dimension n ≥ 0). By definition μHE[n] = κ_n • μH[n] on every (e)metric space, with the same constant κ_n = addHaarScalarFactor(volume, μH[n]) ∈ (0, ∞) depending only on n (`euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def`). Multiplying by κ_n: Hⁿ(Φ(B̄)) ≤ Λⁿ · Hⁿ(B̄), where on the right Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝⁿ.

6. (Finiteness.) On ℝⁿ, μHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`), which is finite on the compact set B̄. Therefore Hⁿ(Φ(Ω) ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(Φ(B̄)) ≤ Λⁿ · Lⁿ(B̄) < ∞ (monotonicity of the outer measure Hⁿ). ∎
proof_key_steps: Antilipschitz ⇒ Φ injective on Ω; Lusin–Souslin (continuous injective image of the Borel set Ω) ⇒ Φ(Ω) Borel.
For compact K with Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ≠ ∅, Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) lies in the closed ball B̄ of radius diam(K)/c about a point w₀ ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K).
Φ is C¹, so it is Λ-Lipschitz on the convex compact ball B̄.
Hⁿ(Φ(Ω) ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(Φ(B̄)) ≤ Λⁿ Lⁿ(B̄) < ∞.

subproblems.title: Gram-determinant lower bound c^k ≤ √det(⟨Te_i, Te_j⟩) for a linear map with |Ts| ≥ c|s| (Jacobian bound of step 6a)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let T : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be a continuous linear map (ℝ^m = Eucl m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), and let c ≥ 0 satisfy c|s| ≤ |Ts| for every s ∈ ℝ^k. Let e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin k) and let G := (⟨Te_i, Te_j⟩)_{i,j} be the k×k Gram matrix (Matrix.of). Then c^k ≤ √det G.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (T : Eucl k →L[ℝ] Eucl P) (c : ℝ), 0 ≤ c → (∀ s : Eucl k, c * ‖s‖ ≤ ‖T s‖) → c ^ k ≤ Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (T (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (T (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the Jacobian bound of step (6a) of the parent proof ("the Gram matrix (⟨∂_aΦ(w), ∂_bΦ(w)⟩)_{a,b} is ≥ c²·I, so JΦ(w) ≥ c^k > 0"), isolated for one linear map T. In the parent T = DΦ(w), and the hypothesis |DΦ(w)s| ≥ c|s| is supplied by the sibling fderiv_lower_bound.

Conventions. ℝ^m = Eucl m with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|. e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^k, and x = Σ_i x_i e_i for x ∈ ℝ^k. G_{ij} = ⟨Te_i, Te_j⟩.

1. (Symmetry.) G_{ij} = ⟨Te_i, Te_j⟩ = ⟨Te_j, Te_i⟩ = G_{ji} (real_inner_comm). So the real matrix G is Hermitian: Gᴴ = Gᵀ = G (Matrix.IsHermitian).
2. (Quadratic form.) For x ∈ ℝ^k with coordinates (x_i):
 Σ_i x_i Σ_j G_{ij} x_j = Σ_{i,j} x_i x_j ⟨Te_i, Te_j⟩ = ⟨Σ_i x_i Te_i, Σ_j x_j Te_j⟩ = ⟨Tx, Tx⟩ = |Tx|².
 This uses Tx = Σ_i x_i Te_i (linearity of T) and bilinearity of the real inner product. In matrix notation xᵀGx = |Tx|² (dotProduct x (G.mulVec x)).
3. (Eigenvalues ≥ c².) By the spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices (Mathlib Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvectorBasis, Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues) there is an orthonormal basis u_0, …, u_{k−1} of ℝ^k with Gu_i = λ_i u_i. Moreover λ_i = u_iᵀGu_i (Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues_eq; star and re are the identity on ℝ).
 - By step 2, λ_i = |Tu_i|².
 - By the hypothesis with s = u_i and |u_i| = 1: 0 ≤ c = c|u_i| ≤ |Tu_i|. Hence λ_i = |Tu_i|² ≥ c².
4. (Determinant.) det G = Π_i λ_i (Matrix.IsHermitian.det_eq_prod_eigenvalues). Since 0 ≤ c² ≤ λ_i for every i, Π_i λ_i ≥ Π_i c² = (c²)^k (Finset.prod_le_prod₀).
5. (Square root.) Because c ≥ 0, c^k = √((c^k)²) = √((c²)^k) ≤ √det G, by monotonicity of the square root. ∎

Edge cases are covered by the same argument:
 - k = 0: the matrix is empty, det G = 1 and c^0 = 1 = √1 (empty products in steps 3–4).
 - k > P: T has a nontrivial kernel, so the hypothesis forces c = 0, and step 5 gives 0 ≤ √det G.

subproblems.title: Measurable relative orientation on a C¹ antilipschitz chart: JΦ·ξ(Φ) = σ·simpleNVector(∂Φ) with σ = ±1 (step 6c)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let (M, θ, ξ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ (H^k = μHE[k] on ℝ^P). Let Φ : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be C¹ and c-antilipschitz on an open set Ω ⊆ ℝ^k for some c > 0. Write ∂_bΦ(w) := DΦ(w)e_b (DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w, e_b = EuclideanSpace.single b 1), ∂Φ(w) := (∂_0Φ(w), …, ∂_{k−1}Φ(w)) and JΦ(w) := √det(⟨∂_aΦ(w), ∂_bΦ(w)⟩)_{a,b}. Then there is σ : ℝ^k → ℝ, a.e.-strongly measurable for L^k⌞(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M)) (L^k = volume), such that for L^k-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M): σ(w) ∈ {1, −1} and JΦ(w)·ξ(Φ(w)) = σ(w)·simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)).

Source: step (6c) of the parent proof, together with the measurability of the sign claimed in (6d), for a triple on an arbitrary open U. The parent's ingredients are: good parameters; ξ(x) = ε·simpleNVector τ with span τ = range DΦ(w); simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)) = det B·simpleNVector τ; |det B| = JΦ(w); and the sign built from the covector β_w with β_w(∂Φ(w)) = JΦ(w)². Two harmless changes are made:
 - the sign is σ(w) := 1 if ξ(Φ(w))(β_w) ≥ 0 and σ(w) := −1 otherwise, so σ is ±1 everywhere and no division by JΦ is needed;
 - β_w is written as the pull-back of one fixed covector, which makes w ↦ β_w visibly continuous.

Conventions. H := μHE[k] on ℝ^P; L := volume on ℝ^k; S := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M). For a k-vector N and a k-covector γ, N(γ) is the pairing; simpleNVector v (γ) = γ(v); covectorPullback k A γ = γ(A·, …, A·). † is the Hilbert-space adjoint (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint), and ‖·‖ on k-vectors is the operator norm.

1. (A Borel representative of ξ.) ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞M (field aestronglyMeasurable of the triple). Fix a strongly measurable ξ̃ with ξ = ξ̃ H⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk).
2. (Good points of M ∩ Φ(Ω).) For H⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω))-a.e. y, the following three statements hold.
 (a) For every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = y, range DΦ(w) is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at y. This is the sibling weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart with V := U. Its hypotheses hold: U is open; M ⊆ U, M is H-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, and θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U (the fields subset, nullMeasurableSet, pos and integrableOn of the triple); Ω is open and Φ is C¹ and antilipschitz on Ω.
 (b) There is an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P such that span τ is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at y and ξ(y) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(y) = −simpleNVector τ. This is the field orients, an H⌞M-a.e. statement, restricted to M ∩ Φ(Ω) ⊆ M (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset).
 (c) ξ(y) = ξ̃(y), by step 1 restricted in the same way.
3. (Pull-back to parameters.) Apply the sibling ae_pullback to M, Φ, Ω and the property p(y) := (a) ∧ (b) ∧ (c). Its hypotheses hold: Ω is measurable (open), Φ is measurable (continuous), Φ is antilipschitz on Ω, and M is H-null-measurable. Hence S is L-null-measurable and p(Φ(w)) holds for L⌞S-a.e. w. Moreover L⌞S-a.e. w lies in S (ae_restrict_mem₀).
4. (The test covector.) Let β₀ := wedgeCovectors k (a ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj a), a k-covector on ℝ^k. Let β_w := covectorPullback k (DΦ(w)†) β₀, a k-covector on ℝ^P.
 - Formula. By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, for u = (u_0, …, u_{k−1}) in ℝ^P:
  β_w(u) = det(proj_a(DΦ(w)†u_b))_{a,b} = det(⟨e_a, DΦ(w)†u_b⟩)_{a,b} = det(⟨DΦ(w)e_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b}
  (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left, adjoint_inner_right). In particular β_w(∂Φ(w)) = det(⟨∂_aΦ(w), ∂_bΦ(w)⟩)_{a,b} =: Δ(w).
 - Continuity of w ↦ β_w. w ↦ DΦ(w) is continuous because Φ is C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv); the adjoint is a linear isometry; A ↦ covectorPullback k A is continuous (it is ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM, continuous by ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM); and evaluating a continuous linear map at the fixed β₀ is continuous.
5. (The sign and its measurability.) Put p(w) := ξ(Φ(w))(β_w). Put σ(w) := 1 if p(w) ≥ 0 and σ(w) := −1 if p(w) < 0; so σ(w) ∈ {1, −1} for every w.
 - By step 3(c), w ↦ ξ(Φ(w)) agrees L⌞S-a.e. with w ↦ ξ̃(Φ(w)), which is strongly measurable (ξ̃ strongly measurable, Φ measurable). So it is a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞S.
 - The pairing (N, γ) ↦ N(γ) is bounded bilinear, hence continuous, on NVector × Covector (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply). With step 4, p is a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞S.
 - σ = s∘p with the Borel function s(t) = 1 (t ≥ 0), s(t) = −1 (t < 0). So σ is a.e.-measurable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, for L⌞S.
6. (The identity at good parameters.) Fix w ∈ S at which p(Φ(w)) holds; this is L⌞S-a.e. by step 3. Let x := Φ(w) and v := ∂Φ(w), and let τ be as in 2(b).
 (6.1) θ(x) > 0 since x ∈ M. By 2(a) (with this w) and 2(b), range DΦ(w) and span τ are both weighted approximate tangent spaces of (M, θ) at x. So they are equal (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, which needs θ(x) ≠ 0).
 (6.2) Each v_b = DΦ(w)e_b lies in range DΦ(w) = span τ. So v_b = Σ_a c_a τ_a for some coefficients (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun), and pairing with τ_a gives c_a = ⟨τ_a, v_b⟩ by orthonormality (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype). Let B be the k×k matrix B_{ba} := ⟨τ_a, v_b⟩ (Matrix.of); then v_b = Σ_a B_{ba} τ_a. The second identity of the sibling simple_nvector_algebra gives simpleNVector v = d·simpleNVector τ, where d := det B.
 (6.3) Norms. The first identity of simple_nvector_algebra for τ gives ‖simpleNVector τ‖² = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = det I = 1, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1 (norms are ≥ 0). Hence ‖simpleNVector v‖ = |d|·‖simpleNVector τ‖ = |d|. For k-vectors use the operator-norm inequality ‖r·N‖ ≤ |r|·‖N‖ twice, with r = d and r = d⁻¹; the case d = 0 is direct.
 - The first identity for v gives Δ(w) = ‖simpleNVector v‖² = d². So JΦ(w) = √(d²) = |d|.
 - By step 4, simpleNVector v (β_w) = β_w(v) = Δ(w) = d².
 (6.4) If d = 0, then JΦ(w) = 0 and simpleNVector v = 0. So both sides of JΦ(w)·ξ(x) = σ(w)·simpleNVector v are 0.
 (6.5) If d ≠ 0: from simpleNVector v = d·simpleNVector τ and (6.3), d·simpleNVector τ(β_w) = d². Hence simpleNVector τ(β_w) = d.
  - If ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ, then p(w) = d. So σ(w) = 1 when d > 0 and σ(w) = −1 when d < 0; in both cases |d| = σ(w)·d. Therefore JΦ(w)·ξ(x) = |d|·simpleNVector τ = σ(w)·d·simpleNVector τ = σ(w)·simpleNVector v.
  - If ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ, then p(w) = −d. So σ(w) = 1 when d < 0 and σ(w) = −1 when d > 0; in both cases −|d| = σ(w)·d. Therefore JΦ(w)·ξ(x) = −|d|·simpleNVector τ = σ(w)·d·simpleNVector τ = σ(w)·simpleNVector v.
 Thus σ(w) ∈ {1, −1} and JΦ(w)·ξ(Φ(w)) = σ(w)·simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)) for L⌞S-a.e. w. Together with step 5 this is the assertion. ∎
 For k = 0 every step holds verbatim: Fin 0-families are empty, B is the empty matrix with det B = 1, and JΦ ≡ 1.

subproblems.statement: Let P, Q, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let (M, θ, ξ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ (H^k = μHE[k] on ℝ^P). Let Φ : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be C¹, let Ω ⊆ ℝ^k be open, and let Φ be Lipschitz on Ω and c-antilipschitz on Ω for some c > 0. Let G ⊆ ℝ^P be H^k-null-measurable with G ⊆ M and G ⊆ Φ(Ω), and with θ H^k-integrable on G. Then there is ψ : ℝ^k → ℝ, Lebesgue integrable on Ω, with the following property. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, A : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) and α : ℝ^Q → Covector(ℝ^Q, k) be such that (i) f∘Φ has Fréchet derivative A(Φ(w))∘DΦ(w) at L^k-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(G), and (ii) x ↦ θ(x)·(A(x)_#ξ(x))(α(f(x))) is H^k-integrable on G. Then ∫_G θ(x)·(A(x)_#ξ(x))(α(f(x))) dH^k(x) = ∫_Ω ψ(w)·α(f(Φ(w)))(∂_0(f∘Φ)(w), …, ∂_{k−1}(f∘Φ)(w)) dw. Here A_# = nVectorPushforward k A, DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and ∂_b(f∘Φ)(w) = fderiv ℝ (f∘Φ) w e_b with e_b = EuclideanSpace.single b 1.

Source: steps (6a)–(6d) of the parent proof for one chart, with G := G_K, treating the two integrands at once. About the pair (A, f), (6c)–(6d) only use two facts: (A(x)_#ξ(x))(α(f(x))) is evaluated through ξ(x) = s·JΦ⁻¹·simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)), and A(Φ(w))∂_bΦ(w) = ∂_b(f∘Φ)(w). In the parent this is applied with (f, A) = (g_j, Dg_j) (C¹ chain rule) and with (f, A) = (g, L) (sibling chart_chain_rule). The weight ψ = 1_D·(θ∘Φ)·σ does not depend on (f, A, α).

Conventions. H := μHE[k] on ℝ^P; L := volume on ℝ^k; J := JΦ = √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_a, DΦ(w)e_b⟩)_{a,b}; D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(G); ∂Φ(w) := (DΦ(w)e_b)_b; ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal.

1. (Sets.) D ⊆ Ω, and D ⊆ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) because G ⊆ M.
2. (Jacobian bound, (6a).) Let w ∈ Ω. Φ is differentiable at w (C¹). The sibling fderiv_lower_bound gives c|s| ≤ |DΦ(w)s| for all s. The sibling gram_det_lower_bound with T := DΦ(w) then gives c^k ≤ J(w). In particular J(w) ≥ c^k > 0 on Ω.
3. (Orientation, (6c).) The sibling chart_orientation applies (U open, the triple, Ω open, Φ C¹ and antilipschitz on Ω). It gives σ : ℝ^k → ℝ, a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M)), with σ(w) = ±1 and J(w)·ξ(Φ(w)) = σ(w)·simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)) for L⌞(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M))-a.e. w. By step 1 both facts hold for L⌞D (restriction to a subset: ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset, and AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure with Measure.restrict_mono).
4. (θ on the chart, (6b).) θ is H-integrable on G, so ofReal∘θ is a.e.-measurable for H⌞G. The sibling chart_change_of_variables applies (Ω open, Φ Lipschitz and c-antilipschitz on Ω, G ⊆ Φ(Ω), G null-measurable). It gives:
 - D is L-null-measurable;
 - w ↦ ofReal(θ(Φ(w))) is a.e.-measurable for L⌞D;
 - ∫⁻_G ofReal(θ) dH = ∫⁻_D ofReal(θ(Φ(w)))·ofReal(J(w)) dw.
 For w ∈ D, Φ(w) ∈ G ⊆ M, so θ(Φ(w)) > 0 and θ(Φ(w)) = toReal(ofReal(θ(Φ(w)))). As L⌞D-a.e. w lies in D (ae_restrict_mem₀), θ∘Φ is a.e.-measurable for L⌞D.
5. (The weight.) Put F₁(w) := θ(Φ(w))·σ(w) and ψ := 1_D·F₁ (ψ = F₁ on D and 0 elsewhere). F₁ is a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞D by steps 3–4. D is null-measurable for L⌞Ω, and (L⌞Ω)⌞D = L⌞(D ∩ Ω) = L⌞D (Measure.restrict_restrict₀ and D ⊆ Ω). So ψ is a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞Ω (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff₀).
6. (ψ ∈ L¹(Ω), (6d).) ∫⁻_Ω |ψ| dL = ∫⁻_D |F₁| dL (lintegral_indicator₀ and step 5). For L⌞D-a.e. w we have |σ(w)| = 1 and θ(Φ(w)) > 0, so by step 2
 ofReal|F₁(w)| = ofReal(θ(Φ(w))) = (ofReal c^k)⁻¹·ofReal(θ(Φ(w)))·ofReal(c^k) ≤ (ofReal c^k)⁻¹·ofReal(θ(Φ(w)))·ofReal(J(w)),
 using ofReal c^k ∈ (0, ∞). Integrating (lintegral_mono_ae, lintegral_const_mul'):
 ∫⁻_D |F₁| ≤ (ofReal c^k)⁻¹ ∫⁻_D ofReal(θ∘Φ)·ofReal(J) = (ofReal c^k)⁻¹ ∫⁻_G ofReal(θ) dH ≤ (ofReal c^k)⁻¹ ∫⁻_G |θ| dH < ∞,
 where the equality is step 4. With step 5, ψ is L-integrable on Ω. This is the first conclusion.
7. (The representation.) Let f, A, α satisfy (i) and (ii). Put h(x) := θ(x)·(A(x)_#ξ(x))(α(f(x))) and X(w) := α(f(Φ(w)))(∂_0(f∘Φ)(w), …, ∂_{k−1}(f∘Φ)(w)).
 (7.1) By (ii) and the sibling signed_change_of_variables (same Φ and Ω, with A := G and h := h): ∫_G h dH = ∫_D h(Φ(w))·J(w) dw.
 (7.2) ψ·X = 1_D·(F₁·X). Hence ∫_Ω ψ·X dL = ∫_D F₁·X dL (integral_indicator₀ for L⌞Ω, and (L⌞Ω)⌞D = L⌞D).
 (7.3) For L⌞D-a.e. w, step 3 and (i) hold at w. For such w put x := Φ(w), v := ∂Φ(w) and γ := covectorPullback k (A(x)) (α(f(x))).
  - By definition of the push-forward, (A(x)_#ξ(x))(α(f(x))) = ξ(x)(γ).
  - Evaluating J(w)·ξ(x) = σ(w)·simpleNVector v at γ gives J(w)·ξ(x)(γ) = σ(w)·γ(v), and γ(v) = α(f(x))(A(x)v_0, …, A(x)v_{k−1}) (covectorPullback_apply).
  - By (i), fderiv ℝ (f∘Φ) w = A(x)∘DΦ(w) (HasFDerivAt.fderiv), so ∂_b(f∘Φ)(w) = A(x)(DΦ(w)e_b) = A(x)v_b.
  Hence h(x)·J(w) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(γ)·J(w) = θ(x)·σ(w)·α(f(x))(∂(f∘Φ)(w)) = F₁(w)·X(w).
 (7.4) By (7.3) and setIntegral_congr_ae₀ (D null-measurable), ∫_D h(Φ(w))·J(w) dw = ∫_D F₁·X dL. Combining with (7.1) and (7.2) gives ∫_G h dH = ∫_Ω ψ·X dL, the second conclusion. ∎

subproblems.title: Measurability and tangential bound Λ^k‖β‖θ of push-forward integrands θ·(A_#ξ)(β) on a rectifiable triple (steps 2–3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, Q, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let (M, θ, ξ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ (H^k = μHE[k] on ℝ^P). Let A : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q), β : ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^Q, k) and Λ ∈ ℝ. Assume that x ↦ A(x)_#ξ(x) (A_# = nVectorPushforward k A) and β are a.e.-strongly measurable for H^k⌞M. Assume also that for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M, |A(x)v| ≤ Λ|v| for every v in every weighted approximate tangent space T_x of (M, θ) at x. Then x ↦ θ(x)·(A(x)_#ξ(x))(β(x)) is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^k⌞M, and |θ(x)·(A(x)_#ξ(x))(β(x))| ≤ Λ^k·‖β(x)‖·θ(x) for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M, where ‖β(x)‖ is the operator norm of the covector β(x).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 and 3 of the parent proof (the single dominator, and the measurability of F_j and F), separated from the choice of A. In the parent the lemma is applied twice.
 - A = Dg_j, β = ω∘g_j: |Dg_j(x)v| ≤ Λ′|v| because g_j is Λ′-Lipschitz; measurability of x ↦ Dg_j(x)_#ξ(x) comes from the parent's sibling pushforward_measurable with f = g_j, L = Dg_j.
 - A = L, β = ω∘g: |L(x)v| ≤ Λ|v| on weighted tangent spaces, because t ↦ g(x + tv) is Λ|v|-Lipschitz with derivative L(x)v at 0; measurability again from pushforward_measurable.

Conventions. H := μHE[k] on ℝ^P. Covectors and k-vectors carry operator norms, and |γ(u_0, …, u_{k−1})| ≤ ‖γ‖·Π_a|u_a| for a k-covector γ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).

1. (θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞M.) For q ∈ ℕ let K_q := {x : |x| ≤ q} ∖ thickening(1/(q+1), ℝ^P ∖ U), where thickening(r, E) = {x : dist(x, z) < r for some z ∈ E} is open.
 - K_q is closed and bounded, hence compact.
 - K_q ⊆ U: a point x ∉ U lies in ℝ^P ∖ U ⊆ thickening(1/(q+1), ℝ^P ∖ U).
 - U ⊆ ⋃_q K_q: for x ∈ U choose ε > 0 with B(x, ε) ⊆ U (U is open) and q ∈ ℕ with q ≥ |x| and 1/(q+1) < ε. If x were in thickening(1/(q+1), ℝ^P ∖ U), some z ∉ U would satisfy |x − z| < 1/(q+1) < ε, i.e. z ∈ B(x, ε) ⊆ U, a contradiction. So x ∈ K_q.
 Since M ⊆ U (field subset), M = ⋃_q (M ∩ K_q). By the field integrableOn of the triple, θ is H-integrable, in particular a.e.-strongly measurable, on each M ∩ K_q. For a countable union this gives that θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞M (aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff).
2. (Measurability of the integrand.) The evaluation map NVector(ℝ^Q, k) × Covector(ℝ^Q, k) → ℝ, (N, γ) ↦ N(γ), is bounded bilinear, hence continuous (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply). Composing it with the a.e.-strongly measurable map x ↦ (A(x)_#ξ(x), β(x)) (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk) gives an a.e.-strongly measurable function. Its product with θ (step 1) is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞M. This is the first conclusion.
3. (Good points.) For H⌞M-a.e. x the following hold simultaneously:
 - x ∈ M (ae_restrict_mem₀; M is null-measurable);
 - the orientation clause of the triple gives an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P such that span τ is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x and ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ;
 - the hypothesis on A holds at x.
 Fix such an x.
4. (Bound.) Taking T_x := span τ and v := τ_a ∈ span τ (|τ_a| = 1) in the hypothesis gives |A(x)τ_a| ≤ Λ for every a.
 - By nVectorPushforward_simple, A(x)_#(simpleNVector τ) = simpleNVector(A(x)∘τ), whose value at β(x) is β(x)(A(x)τ_0, …, A(x)τ_{k−1}) (simpleNVector_apply).
 - The push-forward is linear in the vector, so (A(x)_#ξ(x))(β(x)) = ±β(x)(A(x)τ).
 Since 0 ≤ |A(x)τ_a| ≤ Λ for every a (Finset.prod_le_prod₀),
 |(A(x)_#ξ(x))(β(x))| = |β(x)(A(x)τ)| ≤ ‖β(x)‖·Π_a|A(x)τ_a| ≤ ‖β(x)‖·Λ^k.
 For k = 0 the product is empty and equals 1 = Λ⁰.
5. (Conclusion.) θ(x) > 0 because x ∈ M (field pos). So |θ(x)·(A(x)_#ξ(x))(β(x))| = θ(x)·|(A(x)_#ξ(x))(β(x))| ≤ Λ^k·‖β(x)‖·θ(x). This holds for H⌞M-a.e. x, which is the second conclusion. ∎

subproblems.title: Dominated convergence of set integrals along a countable partition (countable additivity and Tannery's theorem; steps 5 and 7)
subproblems.statement: Let (X, μ) be a measure space, let S ⊆ X, and let (E_i)_{i∈ℕ} be pairwise disjoint μ-null-measurable subsets of X with S = ⋃_i E_i μ-almost everywhere. Let G : X → ℝ be μ-integrable on S, and let f_j : X → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ) and f₀ : X → ℝ be a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞S. Assume that |f_j| ≤ G μ⌞S-a.e. for all sufficiently large j, that |f₀| ≤ G μ⌞S-a.e., and that ∫_{E_i} f_j dμ → ∫_{E_i} f₀ dμ as j → ∞ for every i. Then ∫_S f_j dμ → ∫_S f₀ dμ as j → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) (S : Set X) (E : ℕ → Set X) (f : ℕ → X → ℝ) (f₀ G : X → ℝ), (∀ i, NullMeasurableSet (E i) μ) → Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint E) → S =ᵐ[μ] (⋃ i, E i) → IntegrableOn G S μ → (∀ j, AEStronglyMeasurable (f j) (μ.restrict S)) → AEStronglyMeasurable f₀ (μ.restrict S) → (∀ᶠ j in atTop, ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict S), |f j x| ≤ G x) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict S), |f₀ x| ≤ G x) → (∀ i, Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x in E i, f j x ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in E i, f₀ x ∂μ))) → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x in S, f j x ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in S, f₀ x ∂μ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 and 7 of the parent proof (countable additivity over the chart pieces, and dominated convergence for series), stated for an abstract measure space. In the parent: X = ℝ^P, μ = μHE[k], S = M, E_i = the disjointed chart pieces, f_j = F_j, f₀ = F, and G = max(Λ, Λ′)^k·sup‖ω‖·1_{g⁻¹(K)}·θ.

Write S′ := ⋃_i E_i.
1. (Same restricted measure.) Since S = S′ μ-a.e., μ⌞S = μ⌞S′ (Measure.restrict_congr_set), and ∫_S φ dμ = ∫_{S′} φ dμ for every φ (setIntegral_congr_set). In particular G is μ-integrable on S′.
2. (Integrability.) For every j in the eventual range of the bound, f_j is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞S = μ⌞S′ and |f_j| ≤ G a.e. So f_j is μ-integrable on S′ (Integrable.mono'). Likewise f₀ is μ-integrable on S′.
3. (Countable additivity.) The E_i are null-measurable and pairwise disjoint, hence pairwise a.e.-disjoint. For φ integrable on S′, ∫_{S′} φ dμ = Σ_i ∫_{E_i} φ dμ (integral_iUnion_ae). Write a_i(j) := ∫_{E_i} f_j dμ and a_i := ∫_{E_i} f₀ dμ. With steps 1–2:
 - ∫_S f_j dμ = Σ_i a_i(j) for all large j;
 - ∫_S f₀ dμ = Σ_i a_i.
4. (Summable domination.) Let b_i := ∫_{E_i} G dμ. Since G is integrable on S′, Σ_i b_i converges, to ∫_{S′} G dμ (hasSum_integral_iUnion_ae). For each i, μ⌞E_i ≤ μ⌞S′ = μ⌞S (E_i ⊆ S′). So for all large j, |f_j| ≤ G μ⌞E_i-a.e., and |a_i(j)| ≤ b_i (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, with G integrable on E_i).
5. (Tannery.) We have: a_i(j) → a_i for every i (hypothesis); |a_i(j)| ≤ b_i for every i and all large j; and Σ_i b_i < ∞. By dominated convergence for series (Tannery's theorem; Mathlib tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence), Σ_i a_i(j) → Σ_i a_i. By step 3 and eventual equality (Tendsto.congr'), ∫_S f_j dμ → ∫_S f₀ dμ. ∎
